plus.analyst_notes:
Closes https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/issues/23017
Crypto-theft coding convention used throughout this batch: stolen funds coded as confidentiality data variety Virtual currency (data_victim Victim organization unless customer wallets were drained), integrity Fraudulent transaction for the unauthorized transfers, and the USD loss in impact (Asset and fraud). Template Hacking-ext-unknown used. Asset changed to U - Unknown (executives' devices, type not given) plus S - Other (treasury wallets/validator stake on Solana). Action kept as hacking Unknown: Step says only 'a well-known attack vector' compromised execs' devices; secondary write-ups suggest phishing but Step has not said so, so no social/malware action is coded. Credentials coded because control of treasury keys was obtained via the devices.
Data/impact: Step's figure $40M used for impact (CertiK estimate $27-29M). Discovery internal Unknown (Step detected and announced it). Victim country/headcount Unknown. dbir_year 2027. Issue was labeled Needs Details; BleepingComputer added for the device-compromise detail.

event_chain.summary: Executives' devices compromised, vector not disclosed

summary: On January 31, 2026 Solana DeFi portfolio tracker Step Finance said some of its treasury wallets were compromised after attackers compromised devices belonging to its executives through 'a well-known attack vector'. CertiK saw 261,854 SOL (about $27-29 million) unstaked and transferred; Step's own investigation later put losses at about $40 million, of which about $4.7 million was recovered. Step Finance later ceased operations.
